learning_outcomes.text: Acquire a global vision of the operations management system of an industrial company and its interaction with other business functions.
Understand and relate production decisions at the strategic, tactical, and operational levels.
Identify decisions and processes related to the design of production systems.
Reflect on the evolution of market globalization and understand the main current environmental factors influencing operations management in industrial companies.
Analyze the repercussions of technological development on the evolution of production and manufacturing systems.
Become familiar with operations planning, scheduling, and control systems and their application in industry.
Understand the different elements involved in the supply chain and in warehouse and inventory management.

syllabus_topics: THE OPERATIONS SUBSYSTEM AND ITS STRATEGY.
THE DESIGN OF THE OPERATIONS SUBSYSTEM.
teaching_methods: Problem-based learning: Develop active learning through problem-solving that fosters student thinking and/or experimentation, as well as decision-making.
Cooperative learning: Develop active learning through cooperative work strategies among students and fostering shared responsibility to achieve group goals.

Learning contract: Develop active learning through an agreement between the professor and the student specifying what will be learned, how that learning will be monitored, the established time period, and the evaluation criteria.
Case study: Acquisition of learning through the analysis of real or simulated cases, in order to interpret and solve them, training various alternative solution procedures.
Expository/Lecture: Transmit knowledge and activate cognitive processes in the student, involving their participation.
Exercise and problem solving: Practice, rehearse, and apply prior knowledge through routine repetition.
assessment_rules: The final grade is 'Pass' if the final exam score is 5 out of 10 or higher, and each part of the exam exceeds a minimum score of 3 out of 10. A partial exam covering units 1, 2, and 3 can be passed with a grade of 5/10 or higher, provided each part of the partial exceeds 3/10. Passing the partial eliminates this material from the final exam in June. The final exam consists of two blocks: units 1-3 and units 4-6, each with questions and problems. A minimum score of 3/10 is required in all parts. The final grade for the exam is the arithmetic mean of the parts' scores. For extraordinary (July) and special (October) resit exams, there will be a single exam with two parts (exercises and questions), and the partial exam score will not be carried over.
